nodes.name: Every 6h
nodes.notes: ADR-048 Block 4 dead-man's-switch for the zip-inner-images daily-05:00 pg_cron purge ('purge-zip-inner-images', migration 030: once daily 05:00 Warsaw, deletes >12h objects). INDEPENDENT of pg_cron on purpose: if the pg_cron daemon stops entirely, a pg_cron-based watchdog would also be dead and never alert. This n8n schedule is a separate scheduler, so it still fires and catches 'cron silently stopped', 'function errored', 'Vault key missing/invalid' — every failure mode collapses into the same observable symptom: objects older than retention still present. Runs every 6h so a failed purge is caught within ~6h of an object crossing the 40h threshold (healthy ceiling ~36h).

nodes.name: Check now (manual)
nodes.notes: Manual harness to run the staleness check on demand (a Schedule Trigger cannot be fired via the n8n API). Used for Definition-of-Done verification.

parameters.formDescription: Press submit to evaluate zip-inner-images staleness now.

nodes.name: Check Stale Zip Images
nodes.notes: stale = any object in zip-inner-images older than 40h. The purge runs ONCE DAILY at 05:00 Europe/Warsaw deleting >12h objects (migration 030), so a file created in the evening/overnight is <12h old at one 05:00 run and is deleted at the NEXT run — a legitimate lifetime up to ~36h. 40h adds margin so a healthy system never trips; >40h => the daily purge isn't running (cron stopped, function errored, or the Vault key missing/invalid) => WARN.

parameters.query:
select
  count(*) as stale_count,
  coalesce(round(max(extract(epoch from (now() - created_at)) / 3600)::numeric, 1), 0) as oldest_age_hours,
  (count(*) > 0) as stale
from storage.objects
where bucket_id = 'zip-inner-images'
  and created_at < now() - interval '40 hours';

nodes.name: Alert Stale Purge
nodes.notes: Routes a WARN through the centralized Post Alert (v1) seam (ADR-025) — never post to ClickUp directly. Side branch only: the watchdog has no main result to protect, but the seam keeps the channel swappable.
